candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents an initial STEMI (LAD occlusion, ST elevations, elevated troponin) that was treated, followed 2 hours later by fever, sharp retrosternal chest pain, pericardial friction rub, diffuse ST elevations with PR depression/elevation, and no pericardial effusion — classic features of peri-infarction pericarditis. C001 names only the STEMI, which is the underlying cause/component, not the final diagnostic object requested (PIP). The STEMI is a required antecedent but the benchmark specifically asks for the pericarditis complication.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: STEMI is the precipitating event/component of peri-infarction pericarditis, but the benchmark reference is the post-infarction pericarditis complication specifically

case_quality_flags: ECG pattern evolution and friction rub strongly support PIP diagnosis over isolated STEMI
Coronary angiography confirms LAD occlusion as infarct etiology, contextualizing the pericarditis as peri-infarction
